solution:
Let \(f(x) = \cos^{-1}(\sin x)\). Observe that this function is defined for all real numbers. We may rewrite this function as

\(f(x) = \cos^{-1}(\sin x)\)

\(= \cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\) for \(-\dfrac{\pi}{2} \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), since \(\cos^{-1}(\cos t) = t\) only for \(0 \le t \le \pi\)

Thus \(f'(x) = -1\) for \(-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) (on the next interval, \(\dfrac{\pi}{2} < x < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\), the slope is \(+1\); in general \(f'(x) = -\dfrac{\cos x}{|\cos x|}\)).
note: cos^-1(cos(pi/2 - x)) = pi/2 - x only for -pi/2 <= x <= pi/2; the solution stated it for all x.
